To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we demonstrate the phase-resolved electric field of a THz quantum cascade laser (QCL), and we use this to demonstrate that the phase matching between the microwave modulation and THz pulse is a necessary condition for mode locking.

1) we have demonstrated that active mode locking in QCLs requires the phase velocity to equal the group index, and 2) we have demonstrated mode locking and pulse generation in a THz quantum cascade laser (THz-QCL) with a large gain bandwidth (500 GHz).

the synchronization between the phase velocity of microwave modulation and the group velocity of THz pulses in quantum cascade lasers ( QCL s) is necessary for the generation of ultrashhort THz pulses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
generating ultrafast pulses of radiation using quantum cascade lasers (QCIs).
the generation of ultrashhort optical pulses using quantum cascade lasers (see figure).
the study of ultrafast phenomena in the mid-infrared and terahertz regions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mode locking in QCLs is a result of the synchronization of the propagating microwave round-trip and the THz pulse, which is the key for pulse generation in QCLs.
the synchronization between the microwave round-tript modulation and the THz pulses is the dominant factor in the generation of ultrafast pulses in QCLs.
the generation of ultrashhort pulses from quantum cascade laser is possible by synchronizing the propagating electron modulation with the generated terahertz (Thz) pulse in the quantum cascade laser.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that the phase matching between the microwave round-trips and the generated THZ pulse is the key factor for the active mode locking of QCLs.
we demonstrate that active THz pulse generation in QCLs is possible and we provide the mechanism for the generation.
the synchronization of the phase velocity of microwave modulation and group velocity of THz pulses is the dominant factor for active mode locking and short pulse generation in QCLs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the phase velocity of round-trip microwave modulation must match the group velocity of THz pulse propagation for active mode locking to occur.
the phase velocity of a round trip microwave modulation should equal the group velocity for THz pulse generation in QCLs.
the generation of ultrafast pulses from QCLs is possible and can be achieved by synchronizing the phase velocity of a microwave round-trip signal with the phase velocity of THz pulse in a QCL.
